To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The XMM-Bright Survey, a flux-limited X-ray survey, is the most complete X-ray survey of its kind.

(1) The XMM-Newton survey is sampling a population of X-ray sources dominated by AGN, with a fraction of absorbed objects larger than expected; (2) The XMM-BSS and XMM-HBSS are the largest and deepest samples of spectroscopically confirmed X-ray selected AGN in the X-ray sky.

the BSS and HBSS samples are the largest and most complete XMM-Newton source samples available so far, that the majority of the sources have an optical counterpart with magnitude fainter than the POSS II R limit and that the majority of them are AGN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the X-ray sky and, in particular, with the properties of the X-ray source population at fluxes of similar to7 x 10-14 erg cm(-2)s(-1) and above in the 0-7.5keV energy band.
the X-ray emission from the most common type of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), namely, Seyfert 1 galaxies, which have a bright nucleus and a large, broad emission-line region.

a detailed study of a sample of 400 bright X-ray sources, with flux limit f(x) similar to7 x 10(14) erg cm(2) s(-)1, in the 0-4.5 and 4.6-7.6 keV energy bands, derived from 237 XMM-Newton observations, with the goal of providing a detailed analysis of the X-ray properties of this sample and to identify their counterparts at other wavelengths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XMM- Newton Bright Serendipitious Survey is the largest and deepest X-ray flux-limited survey in the sky, with the highest percentage of identified X-ray objects.
the XMM- Newton Bright Source Sample and the XMM-Newtown "Hard" Bright Sample are the most complete, homogeneous and reliable X-ray flux-limited samples available in the XMM- Newtow catalog.

the XMM- Newton bright surveys are providing us with a wealth of information about AGN and their environments, and that these surveys will be the cornerstone for future studies on X-ray surveys and AGN evolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are now able to study the properties of the AGN populations at a flux level similar to the one of the 2-10 keV ROSAT Bright Survey Sample (BSS) and the X-ray luminosity of the BSS is similar to 1/3 of that of the ROSAT BSS.
we have provided a solid basis for the XMM- Newton community to use the X-ray sky in a more efficient way, in order to study the most interesting X-ray source populations.

the BSS (and the HBSS) is now a unique and complete sample of X-ray sources that can be used to address several important astrophysical issues such as: the nature of the cosmic X- ray background, the nature of the AGN population, the X-ray properties of the starburst galaxies, the nature of obscured AGN and the nature of the Galactic X-ray emitting population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the energy range of XMM-Newton, a significant fraction of the X-ray sources detected at high Galactic latitudes is indeed an extragalactic source.
the XMM- Newton Bright Source Sample (and its "harder" version, the Hard XMM-Newton Source Sample) is a well-defined and well-behaved flux-limited survey of the X-ray Universe.
the BSS and HBSS samples can be used as a "reference sample" of AGN for a large variety of studies.
